questions.question: Because there is always some degree of processing and network latency involved, real-time analytics is also known as what?
options: Batch analytics
Near real-time analytics
Snapshot analytics
Historical analytics
questions.explanation: M3.1 states that real-time analytics is also known as near real-time analytics, since there is always some degree of processing and network latency involved.

questions.question: In Real-Time Intelligence, what is a stream?
options: A static snapshot of historical data stored in a database
A single digital record or log entry that documents an activity
A sequence of events, typically ordered by the time an event occurred
A scheduled batch job that processes data overnight
questions.explanation: M3.1 defines a stream as essentially a sequence of events, typically ordered by the time an event occurred, that flows continuously as events occur.

questions.question: Which Real-Time Intelligence component is used to store streaming data in KQL (Kusto Query Language) databases?
options: Eventhouse
Real-Time hub
Activator
KQL Queryset
questions.explanation: M3.1 says Real-Time Intelligence stores data in KQL databases in Eventhouses, which are designed for time-series data and fast ingestion of streaming data.

questions.question: What is the primary purpose of the Real-Time hub in Microsoft Fabric?
options: To store KQL databases for real-time analytics
To discover and manage all of the data-in-motion you have access to
To run automated actions when rule thresholds are met
To transform streaming data before routing it to destinations
questions.explanation: M3.1 describes the Fabric Real-Time hub as a central location where you can discover and manage all of the data-in-motion you have access to, serving as a streaming data catalog.

questions.question: According to M3.1, what can Eventstreams do with data as it flows through the system?
options: Only store data, with no processing capabilities
Filter, enrich, and transform data and route it to different destinations
Run management commands such as update policies
Visualize data in interactive dashboards
questions.explanation: M3.1 states that Eventstreams capture streaming data from various sources and apply real-time transformations, allowing them to filter, enrich, and transform data and route it to different destinations.

questions.question: In addition to Kusto Query Language (KQL), which query language does the KQL Queryset support for data analysis?
options: Spark SQL
DAX
T-SQL
M Query
questions.explanation: M3.1 states that the KQL Queryset also supports T-SQL queries, allowing you to use familiar SQL syntax alongside KQL for data analysis.

questions.question: Which of the following can Activator trigger when configured rule conditions are met?
options: Only email notifications
Send notifications, trigger workflows in Power Automate, and execute Fabric data pipelines or notebooks
Create new KQL databases in Eventhouses
Ingest data from Azure Event Hubs
questions.explanation: M3.1 says Activator can send notifications, trigger workflows in Power Automate, and execute Fabric data pipelines or notebooks when conditions are met.

questions.question: What do Real-Time Dashboards connect to directly, and how do they update?
options: They connect to Lakehouses and update on a nightly schedule
They connect to KQL databases and refresh automatically as new data arrives
They connect to the Real-Time hub and require manual refresh
They connect to Power BI datasets and update hourly
questions.explanation: M3.1 states Real-Time Dashboards connect directly to KQL databases and refresh automatically as new data arrives, letting you explore data interactively and monitor current conditions and historical trends.

questions.question: According to M3.1, when are update policies in a KQL database triggered, and what do they do?
options: They run on a scheduled interval and delete old data
They are triggered when new data is written to a table, running a query that transforms the ingested data and saves the result to a destination table
They are applied during eventstream transformations before routing to a destination
They trigger external workflows in Power Automate
questions.explanation: M3.1 says update policies are automation mechanisms triggered when new data is written to a table; they run a query to transform ingested data and save the result to a destination table.

questions.question: What is the eventstream canvas in Microsoft Fabric?
options: A command-line tool for writing stream processing code
A visual editor where you design pipelines by dragging and dropping nodes such as sources, transformations, and destinations
A storage container for KQL databases
A dashboard for visualizing streaming data
questions.explanation: M3.2 says you can use the eventstream canvas, a visual editor, to design your pipeline by dragging and dropping different nodes, such as sources, transformations, and destinations, without writing code.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT listed as a no-code transformation available in Eventstream?
options: Filter
Manage fields
Aggregate
Machine learning model training
questions.explanation: M3.2 lists no-code transformations including Filter, Manage fields, Aggregate, Group by, Union, Join, Expand, and SQL code; machine learning model training is not one of them.

questions.question: What is the purpose of a derived stream destination in an eventstream?
options: To store processed data in Delta Lake format
To enable content-based routing of subsets of data to different destinations
To trigger actions based on detected patterns in streaming data
To ingest data from external systems outside Microsoft Fabric
questions.explanation: M3.2 says derived streams are transformed versions of your original data stream that enable content-based routing, letting you route subsets of data to different destinations based on the content of data.

questions.question: Which of the following is a valid eventstream destination in Microsoft Fabric?
options: Azure Blob Storage event
Custom endpoint
Kafka topic
Real-Time hub
questions.explanation: M3.2 lists eventstream destinations as Eventhouse, Lakehouse, derived stream, Fabric Activator, and custom endpoint. Azure Blob Storage events and Kafka topics are sources, not destinations.

questions.question: How does the Union transformation handle events from two or more nodes?
options: It combines events with shared fields of the same name and data type, dropping fields that don't match
It joins events based on a matching condition between streams
It creates a new row for each value within an array
It aggregates events over time windows
questions.explanation: M3.2 says the union transformation connects two or more nodes and adds events with shared fields (with the same name and data type) into one table; fields that don't match are dropped.

questions.question: Which operations does the Aggregate transformation in Eventstream support?
options: Sum, Minimum, Maximum, or Average
Count and distinct only
Union and join
Filter and manage fields
questions.explanation: M3.2 states the aggregate transformation calculates an aggregation (Sum, Minimum, Maximum, or Average) every time a new event occurs over a period of time.

questions.question: What time window types does the Group by transformation support?
options: Fixed intervals only
Overlapping intervals only
Tumbling windows (fixed intervals) and sliding windows (overlapping intervals)
Sliding windows and event-time windows only
questions.explanation: M3.2 says the group by transformation supports various time windows including tumbling windows (fixed intervals) and sliding windows (overlapping intervals).

questions.question: When routing real-time data to a Lakehouse destination in an eventstream, what happens to the events?
options: They are stored as raw JSON files
They are converted into Delta Lake format and then stored in designated lakehouse tables
They are loaded directly into a KQL database
They are sent to a custom endpoint outside Fabric
questions.explanation: M3.2 says with a Lakehouse destination, real-time events are converted into Delta Lake format and then stored in designated lakehouse tables.

questions.question: Which eventstream destination is useful when you want to direct real-time data to an external system or custom application outside Microsoft Fabric?
options: Eventhouse
Derived stream
Fabric Activator
Custom endpoint
questions.explanation: M3.2 explains the custom endpoint destination lets you route real-time events to a custom endpoint, useful when directing real-time data to an external system or custom application outside Microsoft Fabric.

questions.question: How do KQL databases in an Eventhouse organize incoming data for query performance?
options: By partitioning data by ingestion time
By partitioning data alphabetically by table name
By storing all data in a single unpartitioned store
By partitioning data by data type
questions.explanation: M3.3 says KQL databases automatically partition data by ingestion time, making recent data quickly accessible while storing historical data for trend analysis.

questions.question: Why is real-time data in an Eventhouse described as time-series data?
options: Because it is frequently updated and deleted
Because events are immutable and permanently tied to when they happened, following an append-only pattern
Because data is randomly reordered after ingestion
Because timestamps are optional metadata
questions.explanation: M3.3 explains that real-time data represents immutable events that happened at specific moments; since each event is permanently tied to when it happened, data follows an append-only pattern where it is rarely updated or deleted.

questions.question: Which of the following statements about KQL is true?
options: KQL is case-insensitive for table names and column names
KQL is case-sensitive for everything including table names, column names, function names, operators, keywords, and string values
KQL only supports table names and not operators
KQL treats TaxiTrips, taxitrips, and TAXITRIPS as the same identifier
questions.explanation: M3.3 notes that KQL is case-sensitive for everything including table names, column names, function names, operators, keywords, and string values, so TaxiTrips is different from taxitrips.

questions.question: What do database shortcuts to KQL databases in other eventhouses or Azure Data Explorer allow you to do?
options: Copy data into your eventhouse for local storage
Query data from external KQL databases as if the data were stored locally, without actually copying the data
Merge external data into your local tables
Create materialized views from external data
questions.explanation: M3.3 says database shortcuts let you query data from external KQL databases as if the data were stored locally in your eventhouse, without actually copying the data.

questions.question: What does enabling OneLake availability for a KQL database or table enable?
options: Automated alerting with Activator
Cross-workload integration with Power BI, Warehouse, Lakehouse, and other Fabric services
Direct ingestion from Apache Kafka
Querying data with T-SQL
questions.explanation: M3.3 says you can enable OneLake availability for individual KQL databases or tables, making your data accessible throughout the Fabric ecosystem for cross-workload integration with Power BI, Warehouse, Lakehouse, and other Fabric services.

questions.question: What are the two parts of a materialized view that work together to provide always-current results?
options: A source table and a destination table
A materialized part (precomputed aggregations) and a delta (new data since the last background update)
An update policy and a stored function
A tumbling window and a sliding window
questions.explanation: M3.3 says a materialized view consists of a materialized part with precomputed aggregation results and a delta containing new data that has arrived since the last background update.

questions.question: How are materialized views created in a KQL database?
options: With a .create materialized-view command that encapsulates a KQL summarize statement
With a .create-or-alter function command
With a T-SQL SELECT statement
By dragging a transformation onto the eventstream canvas
questions.explanation: M3.3 shows that a materialized view is created with the .create materialized-view command and encapsulates a KQL summarize statement that automatically updates as new data arrives.

questions.question: What is the main benefit of stored functions in an eventhouse?
options: They precompute aggregation results for faster queries
They encapsulate a query so common filtering or transformation logic can be defined once and reused consistently across queries
They automatically partition data by ingestion time
They provide real-time visualizations
questions.explanation: M3.3 says stored functions let you encapsulate a query, optionally with parameters, so you can define filtering or transformation logic once and reuse it, ensuring calculations are performed consistently.

questions.question: What is the key principle of query optimization in KQL databases described in M3.3?
options: The more columns you project, the faster the query
The less data your query needs to process, the faster it runs
Joins should always start with the largest table
Aggregations should always be performed before filtering
questions.explanation: M3.3 states the key principle is that the less data your query needs to process, the faster it runs, and advises filtering early and reducing columns to improve performance.

questions.question: What data source do Real-Time Dashboards in Microsoft Fabric connect to?
options: Power BI semantic models
KQL databases in eventhouses
OneLake Delta tables only
Lakehouse warehouses
questions.explanation: M3.4 says Real-Time Dashboards connect to KQL databases in eventhouses and display visualizations that refresh automatically to show current data.

questions.question: What are the two identity options you can specify when connecting a Real-Time Dashboard to a data source?
options: Pass-through identity and dashboard editor's identity
Read-only identity and write identity
Service principal and user identity
Anonymous identity and authenticated identity
questions.explanation: M3.4 describes two authorization options: pass-through identity, where each viewer accesses data using their own permissions, and the dashboard editor's identity, where everyone uses the creator's permissions.

questions.question: How does a newly created tile display the results of its KQL query by default?
options: As a bar chart
As a map
As a table
As a line chart
questions.explanation: M3.4 states that initially the tile displays the results of the query as a table, and you can later edit the tile to define a chart, map, or other visualization.

questions.question: What are pages used for in a Real-Time Dashboard?
options: To store multiple base queries
To organize related tiles into logical groups, such as separate pages for different data sources or subject areas
To define parameters for filtering data
To set the automatic refresh rate
questions.explanation: M3.4 says you can add more pages as containers for more tiles, helping you organize related content into logical groups such as different data sources or subject areas.

questions.question: How are dashboard parameters referenced within tile queries?
options: With a dollar sign prefix
With an underscore prefix on the variable name
With curly braces around the variable name
With an @ symbol prefix
questions.explanation: M3.4 says each parameter has a variable name that you reference in tile queries using an underscore prefix, such as _selected_neighbourhoods.

questions.question: How does auto refresh work in a Real-Time Dashboard?
options: Viewers always use the editor's default refresh rate
Editors set a default refresh rate, viewers can adjust it during their session, and editors can set a minimum rate to manage system performance
Refresh happens only once per day
Only the dashboard editor can trigger refresh manually
questions.explanation: M3.4 says editors can set a default refresh rate, viewers can adjust the rate during their session, and editors can set a minimum refresh rate to manage system performance.

questions.question: What is the purpose of base queries in a Real-Time Dashboard?
options: To define multiple parameters for filtering
To retrieve a general set of records relevant for multiple tiles, avoiding duplicate query logic across tiles
To set the dashboard refresh rate
To configure pass-through identity
questions.explanation: M3.4 says base queries retrieve a general set of records relevant for multiple tiles, and tile-specific queries filter or group this data, helping avoid duplicating the same logic.

questions.question: Besides data visualization tiles, what other type of tile can you add to a Real-Time Dashboard?
options: Text tiles to provide additional information
KQL queryset tiles
Eventstream source tiles
Activator rule tiles
questions.explanation: M3.4 states you can add multiple tiles to a dashboard and arrange them, and you can also add text tiles to provide additional information.

questions.question: In the example tile query from M3.4, what does the arg_max(ingestion_time(), *) summarize expression retrieve for each neighborhood?
options: The sum of all bike observations in the last 30 minutes
The most recent observation (the latest record ingested) within the last 30 minutes for each neighborhood
The average number of empty docks across all neighborhoods
The total count of records ingested in the last hour
questions.explanation: M3.4 explains that the example query retrieves the most recent observation (the latest record ingested into the source table) within the last 30 minutes for each neighborhood.

questions.question: What does Activator refer to in Microsoft Fabric?
options: A data visualization tool for dashboards
Microsoft Fabric's event detection and rules engine within Real-Time Intelligence
A KQL query editor
A data ingestion connector
questions.explanation: M3.5 defines Activator as Microsoft Fabric's event detection and rules engine within Real-Time Intelligence.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT one of the four types of actions offered by Activator?
options: Email actions
Teams actions
Power Automate actions
SMS text message actions
questions.explanation: M3.5 lists the four action types as Email, Teams, Power Automate, and Fabric item actions; SMS text messages are not listed as an Activator action type.

questions.question: In the Activator business objects model, what do objects, properties, and events represent?
options: Objects are data attributes, properties are instances, and events contain rules
Objects represent individual instances, properties represent data attributes for each instance, and events contain the actual data values that flow in from data sources
Objects are eventstreams, properties are destinations, and events are transformations
Objects are alerts, properties are actions, and events are thresholds
questions.explanation: M3.5 explains that objects represent individual instances (like Package001), properties represent data attributes for each instance (like Temperature), and events contain the actual data values that flow in from data sources.

questions.question: When creating business objects from an eventstream, which field should you select as the unique identifier?
options: The timestamp field
The field that uniquely identifies the object, such as PackageId or DeviceID
The temperature field
The city field
questions.explanation: M3.5 says during object creation you choose your unique identifier by selecting the field that uniquely identifies the object, like PackageId or DeviceID.

questions.question: Which summarization options does Activator offer when monitoring an attribute?
options: Average, Minimum/Maximum, Count, and Total
Sum, Percentile, Median, and Standard deviation
Filter, Group by, Union, and Join
Window size and step size only
questions.explanation: M3.5 lists the summarization options as Average, Minimum/Maximum, Count, and Total, used to smooth out noise in raw readings.

questions.question: Which of the following is a detection approach offered in the Condition section of an Activator rule?
options: Pattern recognition
Missing data
Anomaly scoring
Forecast comparison
questions.explanation: M3.5 lists detection approaches including threshold monitoring, change detection, range monitoring, and missing data (for catching sensor failures).

questions.question: In an Activator rule, what is the difference between the 'Every time' and 'When it has been true for' occurrence behaviors?
options: 'Every time' triggers for immediate alerts, while 'When it has been true for' identifies persistent problems
'Every time' identifies persistent problems, while 'When it has been true for' sends immediate alerts
Both always trigger the same way
'Every time' is only used for email actions
questions.explanation: M3.5 says 'Every time' is used for immediate alerts, while 'When it has been true for' is used to identify persistent problems, such as a condition staying high for 15 minutes.

questions.question: How many filters can you combine in the Property filter section of an Activator rule?
options: One
Two
Three
Five
questions.explanation: M3.5 says you can combine up to three filters in the Property filter section to create precise targeting of which events get evaluated.

questions.question: Besides the business objects model, which alternative alerting approaches does the Activator engine support?
options: Dashboard alerts, system event alerts, and query alerts
Power BI alerts, dataflow alerts, and pipeline alerts
Email alerts, Teams alerts, and SMS alerts
Eventstream alerts, KQL database alerts, and lakehouse alerts
questions.explanation: M3.5 says the Activator engine also supports creating dashboard alerts from Real-Time Dashboard visualizations, system event alerts for Fabric workspace activities and OneLake file operations, and query alerts from KQL Queryset results.
